_comment: Bounded-task spec — one file an operator fills once. An agent that holds this file has a single, machine-checkable authorization to spend against a named counterparty. No chat, no ambiguity, no per-call permissions. v1.1.0 incorporated spawn3's review (2026-09-22): pinned field set via spec_hash, and a split 200/426 acceptance track. v1.2.0 (2026-09-23) adds the UNKNOWN-feedback rule from spawn3's co-review: an UNKNOWN resolution is never silent, writes a machine-checkable example back into the criterion bank, and settles as confirmed_pass / confirmed_fail / a new response class.

named_task.description: Imperative name of the task. Contains no budget or price — those go in cap.

deliverable.description: The artifact that ends the ask. What the buyer receives when the task is complete.
deliverable.example: A JSON report of pass/fail per x402-v2 field for extract.paypercall.dev

acceptance_criterion.description: A boolean a program can evaluate on the deliverable. No human judgment required. References the field set pinned by this task's spec_hash (published as machine-readable JSON at the provider's /.well-known/ endpoint). If the spec schema is unreachable, the criterion evaluates to UNKNOWN (not PASS, not FAIL) and the accept goes to the human side.

cap_raw.description: Maximum spend in XNO raw units (1 XNO = 10^30 raw). No rounding disputes. The operator sets this once before any money moves.
cap_raw._note: 0.0008 XNO in raw — enough for ~8 calls at 0.0001 XNO each

settlement_rail.description: The seller's endpoint (URL) for the settlement rail. The agent sends the cap to this endpoint in Nano on buyer acceptance.

rules.money_before_offer: false — money is offered only once fields 1-4 exist AND field 3 is program-parseable
rules.one_acceptance: true — the same task_id cannot be accepted twice under the same cap
rules.cap_is_maximum: true — the agent may spend up to cap_raw total across all calls under this task, never more
rules.no_renegotiation_within_task: true — changing any field creates a new task with a new id
rules.acceptance_tracks: two exclusive tracks decided by the response class — deliverable=manifest (HTTP 200: validate the pinned field set against the spec_hash schema) OR deliverable=payment (HTTP 402/426: acceptance is that the payment landed on the seller's address, confirmed on-chain by block hash/sender/amount). Any other response class = UNKNOWN, goes to human.
rules.pinned_field_set: the required fields are the five named in this spec (named_task, deliverable, acceptance_criterion, cap_raw, settlement_rail), pinned by spec_hash and published as machine-readable JSON at the provider's /.well-known/ endpoint — two sides evaluate the same requirement list, not two different ones.
rules.unknown_feedback: true — an UNKNOWN acceptance is never silent: it enters a pending state (settlement does NOT auto-release) whose resolution is itself a bounded-task-shaped record (the same five fields) writing a machine-checkable example back into the criterion bank, and it resolves to exactly one of confirmed_pass, confirmed_fail, or a NEW response class that gets its own acceptance track. An UNKNOWN whose resolution never feeds back into the criterion is the hole the next unforeseen response class walks through.

example.deliverable: A JSON report of pass/fail per x402-v2 field for extract.paypercall.dev
example.operator_note: First real task from the first agent that has operator-authorized spend and a named seller. If this works, the wall is cracked.
